text.p: Italian bond futures held at lower levels reflecting the slide in the lira against the mark and weakness in German bunds, but there was uncertainty as investors pondered the market's next move, dealers said.
They said that domestic investors were heavy sellers in early trading, but there was general unease as the lira slid while U.S. T-bonds attempted to hold steady levels.

Dealers said that the lira's fall continued today after the comments by Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Tuesday that the Italian currency was slightly too strong, which sent it sliding down in late trade yesterday.
Later today, Prodi said he was not worried about the lira and denied that he had said the currency had become too strong.
Dealers said that there could have been some lightening of bond positions ahead of BTP auctions on Thursday and Friday.
